## Load the data

```{r load-data}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Task 1

```{r task1}
# How many listings each host has
host_counts = listings |>
  dplyr::count(host_id, name = "host_listings")

# A1
host_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(host_listings >= 10) |>
  dplyr::summarize(hosts_10_plus = dplyr::n())

# Join the count back onto every listing
listings_hosts = listings |>
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# A2
listings_hosts |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(pct_big_hosts = round(100 * mean(host_listings >= 10), 1))
```

## Task 2

```{r task2}
family_value = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt",
                accommodates >= 4,
                number_of_reviews >= 10,
                review_scores_rating >= 4.8) |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |>
  dplyr::summarize(median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person),
                   n_listings = dplyr::n(),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n_listings >= 20)

# A3: Columbus cheapest per person first
family_value |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::arrange(median_price_per_person)
```

## Task 3

```{r task3}
earnings = listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |>
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
                                 ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                   .groups = "drop")

earnings
```

## Task 4

```{r task4}
concentration = listings |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::mutate(top_10_pct = dplyr::row_number() <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())) |>
  dplyr::summarize(pct_revenue_top_10 = round(100 * sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[top_10_pct]) /
                                                 sum(estimated_revenue_l365d), 1))

concentration
```

## Task 5

```{r task5}
october = availability |>
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10")

year_ahead = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(october, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(pct_mostly_taken = round(100 * mean(mostly_taken), 1),
                   n_homes = dplyr::n()) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pct_mostly_taken)

year_ahead
```

## Task 6

```{r task6}
demand = reviews |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(listings, id, city), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::filter(month >= "2025-07", month <= "2026-06") |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |>
  dplyr::summarize(total_reviews = sum(reviews), .groups = "drop")

# Twin Cities businest month first
twin_cities = demand |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))

twin_cities

# A8 and A9
twin_cities |>
  dplyr::summarize(busiest_month = month[which.max(total_reviews)],
                   ratio_busiest_to_quietest = round(max(total_reviews) / min(total_reviews), 2))
```

## Task 7

```{r task7}
superhost = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt",
                !is.na(host_is_superhost)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |>
  dplyr::summarize(median_price = median(price),
                   median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
                   median_reviews_per_month = median(reviews_per_month, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n_homes = dplyr::n(),
                   .groups = "drop")

superhost

# Premim: superhost median price minus otherhost median price
premium = superhost |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(premium = median_price[host_is_superhost == "t"] -
                             median_price[host_is_superhost == "f"])

premium
```

## Task 8

```{r task8}
lost = listings |>
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id")

# A10: listings with no rows in availability
lost |>
  dplyr::summarize(n_lost = dplyr::n())

# Which city loses the most 
lost |>
  dplyr::count(city, sort = TRUE)
```
